questions.question: Which of the following was an immediate territorial outcome of the Spanish-American War under the 1898 Treaty of Paris?
options: The United States purchased Alaska and Hawaii directly from the Spanish crown
The United States acquired Puerto Rico, Guam, and the Philippines from Spain, while Cuba attained nominal independence subject to U.S. oversight
Spain retained sovereignty over the Philippines in exchange for relinquishing all Caribbean claims
The United States surrendered its naval claims in Guantanamo Bay
questions.explanation: The 'splendid little war' marked America's emergence as an overseas imperial power. Under the Treaty of Paris (1898), Spain ceded Puerto Rico, Guam, and sold the Philippines for $20 million. Cuba gained independence, but the Platt Amendment gave the US right of military intervention.
questions.citation: College Board AP® U.S. History CED — Unit 7: Topic 7.2 Imperialism: Debates

questions.question: The publication of Upton Sinclair's 1906 novel The Jungle contributed most directly to which federal legislative reform under President Theodore Roosevelt?
options: The passage of the Pure Food and Drug Act and the Meat Inspection Act of 1906
The establishment of the Federal Reserve banking system
The passage of the Clayton Antitrust Act protecting labor unions from prosecution
The ratification of the Eighteenth Amendment establishing national Prohibition
questions.explanation: Although Sinclair intended to generate public sympathy for exploited socialist factory workers, readers were horrified by his visceral descriptions of unsanitary Chicago meatpacking plants. President Theodore Roosevelt investigated and pushed Congress to pass the Meat Inspection Act and Pure Food and Drug Act.
questions.citation: College Board AP® U.S. History CED — Unit 7: Topic 7.4 The Progressives

questions.subtopic: WWI & The League of Nations Debate (Period 7: 1890–1945)
questions.question: Why did the United States Senate, led by Senator Henry Cabot Lodge, ultimately reject the Treaty of Versailles in 1919 and 1920?
options: President Woodrow Wilson refused to grant women the right to vote in the treaty text
The treaty failed to impose any financial war reparations upon Germany
The treaty granted Great Britain exclusive sovereign control over the Panama Canal
Senators feared that Article X of the League of Nations Covenant would draw the U.S. into foreign wars without the constitutional consent of Congress
questions.explanation: Article X of the League Covenant pledged member nations to respect and preserve the territorial integrity of all members against external aggression. 'Reservationists' (led by Lodge) and 'Irreconcilables' feared this collective security clause infringed upon Congress's constitutional authority to declare war.
questions.citation: College Board AP® U.S. History CED — Unit 7: Topic 7.6 World War I: Home Front and Aftermath

questions.question: The Palmer Raids of 1919–1920 and the Immigration Act of 1924 (National Origins Act) reflected which pervasive post-World War I societal sentiment?
options: A broad national consensus favoring open borders to satisfy post-war industrial labor shortages
A bipartisan rejection of protective tariffs and a revival of free trade internationalism
A surge in nativism and anti-radical hysteria fueled by fears of Bolshevik communism and foreign anarchist revolutions
A universal federal commitment to desegregate public accommodations in urban centers
questions.explanation: Following the 1917 Bolshevik Revolution and mail-bomb attacks in 1919, Attorney General A. Mitchell Palmer directed raids arresting and deporting suspected radical immigrants without warrants. This nativist climate culminated in the National Origins Act of 1924, establishing strict nationality quotas targeting Southern and Eastern Europeans.

questions.question: The Harlem Renaissance of the 1920s is best characterized as:
options: A vibrant literary, musical, and artistic flourishing that celebrated African American cultural identity and challenged racial stereotypes
A mass migration movement advocating for the physical return of African Americans to Liberia
A political party that won legislative majorities across northern urban districts
An exclusively religious crusade that sought to establish independent churches in the rural South
questions.explanation: Fueled by the Great Migration, Harlem became the vibrant cultural capital of Black America. Figures like Langston Hughes, Zora Neale Hurston, Duke Ellington, and Louis Armstrong produced groundbreaking literature, poetry, and jazz that expressed Black pride, resilience, and resistance to white racism.

questions.question: Which of the following was a primary structural cause of the Great Depression preceding the stock market crash of October 1929?
options: The complete absence of protective tariffs on imported foreign goods
Excessive consumer credit speculation, severe income inequality, and agricultural overproduction resulting in chronically depressed commodity prices
Overly generous federal social welfare expenditures that bankrupted the national treasury
A dramatic shortage of manufactured industrial goods relative to consumer demand
questions.explanation: Beneath 1920s prosperity lay deep structural weaknesses: American farmers had suffered from overproduction and plummeting prices since WWI; wealth was intensely concentrated; consumers relied on installment debt; and banks engaged in reckless, unregulated margin lending for stock speculation.

questions.question: The Social Security Act of 1935 represented a fundamental transformation in American governance primarily because it:
options: Nationalized all private commercial banks and placed them under federal ownership
Guaranteed every American citizen a federally subsidized home mortgage
Established a permanent federal responsibility to provide a social safety net, including old-age pensions, unemployment insurance, and aid to dependent children
Abolished all private employer pension plans in favor of military-style pensions
questions.explanation: A cornerstone of the Second New Deal, the Social Security Act marked a dramatic shift from laissez-faire governance to the modern American welfare state, codifying the federal government's legal duty to safeguard citizens against the economic hazards of old age, disability, and unemployment.

questions.question: What was the constitutional significance of the Supreme Court's decision in Korematsu v. United States (1944)?
options: The Court ruled that President Roosevelt had exceeded his executive authority under Article II
The Court held that citizens of Japanese ancestry were entitled to immediate monetary reparations
The Court struck down the military draft as an unconstitutional violation of the Thirteenth Amendment
The Court upheld the forced internment of over 110,000 Japanese Americans, ruling that wartime military necessity superseded constitutional civil liberties
questions.explanation: In Korematsu v. U.S., Justice Hugo Black wrote for the 6–3 majority that the exclusion and forced internment of Japanese Americans under Executive Order 9066 was a constitutional exercise of emergency wartime powers, despite zero evidence of espionage or disloyalty among the interned population.

questions.question:
“It must be the policy of the United States to support free peoples who are resisting attempted subjugation by armed minorities or by outside pressures.”
— President Harry S. Truman, Address to Congress, March 1947

The policy enunciated in the excerpt became known as the Truman Doctrine and was initially implemented to provide financial and military aid to:
options: South Korea following the invasion by North Korean military forces
Nationalist Chinese forces retreating to Taiwan
West Berlin during the Soviet blockade of road and rail corridors
Greece and Turkey to prevent communist takeovers backed by the Soviet Union
questions.explanation: When Britain announced in 1947 that it could no longer financially support the Greek monarchy against communist insurgents, Truman requested $400 million in aid for Greece and Turkey. This established the Truman Doctrine and containment as the defining framework of American Cold War foreign policy.

questions.question: The European Recovery Program (Marshall Plan) approved by Congress in 1948 aimed primarily to:
options: Establish permanent American colonial protectorates across Central Europe
Rebuild war-torn Western European economies to restore prosperity, stabilize democratic institutions, and blunt the political appeal of communism
Fund the rearmament of the West German military into an independent nuclear force
Force Western European countries to dismantle their national public healthcare systems
questions.explanation: Secretary of State George Marshall proposed spending over $13 billion to reconstruct Western European infrastructure and industry. By revitalizing European commerce, it spurred demand for American goods and eliminated the economic desperation that fostered communist political electoral gains in Italy and France.

questions.question: The Supreme Court's unanimous ruling in Brown v. Board of Education of Topeka (1954), delivered by Chief Justice Earl Warren, held that:
options: Racial quotas must be implemented immediately across all higher education admissions
State legislatures possessed the sovereign right to interpose state authority against federal court orders
Racial segregation in public schools was inherently unequal, violating the Equal Protection Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment
School segregation was constitutional provided both white and black schools received identical per-pupil funding
questions.explanation: Overturning the 1896 Plessy v. Ferguson 'separate but equal' precedent, Chief Justice Earl Warren declared that segregating children in public schools based on race generated feelings of inferiority that could never be undone, establishing that 'separate educational facilities are inherently unequal.'

questions.question: The rapid expansion of suburban housing developments, such as Levittown, in the 1950s was facilitated most directly by:
options: Federal Housing Administration (FHA) and GI Bill low-interest guaranteed mortgages, combined with mass assembly-line home construction and automobile ownership
The complete nationalization of suburban land development by the Department of Housing and Urban Development
The total elimination of racial covenants in all private real estate contracts nationwide
A steep decline in birth rates that reduced household sizes across the country
questions.explanation: The post-WWII baby boom, high union wages, mass-production building techniques (William Levitt), affordable cars, the 1956 Interstate Highway Act, and government-backed FHA and VA mortgage loans made suburban homeownership attainable for millions of white working- and middle-class families.

questions.question: During the Cuban Missile Crisis of October 1962, President John F. Kennedy resolved the dangerous nuclear confrontation with Soviet Premier Nikita Khrushchev by:
options: Launching an immediate preemptive air strike to destroy all Soviet missile sites in Cuba
Ordering a full-scale amphibious military invasion of Havana by U.S. Marines
Imposing a naval 'quarantine' (blockade) of Cuba, while privately agreeing to withdraw American Jupiter missiles from Turkey in exchange for Soviet missile removal from Cuba
Agreeing to surrender West Berlin to the Soviet Union
questions.explanation: Rejecting calls from military chiefs for immediate air strikes or invasion, JFK enacted a naval quarantine around Cuba. In back-channel diplomacy, Khrushchev agreed to dismantle the missiles under UN inspection in exchange for an American public pledge not to invade Cuba and a secret pledge to remove obsolete US missiles from Turkey.

questions.subtopic: Civil Rights Act of 1964 & Voting Rights Act of 1965 (Period 8: 1945–1980)
questions.question: The Voting Rights Act of 1965 dismantled decades of southern voter suppression primarily by:
options: Lowering the federal voting age from twenty-one to eighteen across all states
Requiring all voters to pass a standardized federal civics examination before casting a ballot
Mandating compulsory voting in all federal presidential elections
Outlawing literacy tests and establishing federal oversight and preclearance over voter registration in jurisdictions with historical disenfranchisement
questions.explanation: Catalyzed by the Selma-to-Montgomery march, the Voting Rights Act of 1965 banned literacy tests, authorized federal registrars to register eligible Black voters in counties where discrimination was rampant, and required covered states to get federal 'preclearance' before altering voting procedures.

Medicare (health insurance for elderly Americans) and Medicaid (health coverage for low-income families)
The Civilian Conservation Corps and Works Progress Administration

questions.subtopic: Gulf of Tonkin Resolution & Vietnam War (Period 8: 1945–1980)
questions.question: The Gulf of Tonkin Resolution, passed overwhelmingly by Congress in August 1964, was historically significant because it:
options: Authorized the President to take 'all necessary measures to repel any armed attack', effectively granting LBJ a blank check to escalate U.S. military involvement in Vietnam without a formal declaration of war
Mandated the immediate withdrawal of all American military advisors from South Vietnam
Declared war formally against the Soviet Union and the People's Republic of China
Prohibited the deployment of ground combat troops in mainland Southeast Asia
questions.explanation: Following disputed naval skirmishes in the Gulf of Tonkin, Congress granted Johnson broad executive authority to conduct military operations in Southeast Asia without an official congressional declaration of war, leading to the deployment of over 500,000 ground troops by 1968.

questions.question: Although the January 1968 Tet Offensive was a severe tactical military defeat for the Viet Cong and North Vietnamese Army, it proved to be a decisive psychological turning point in the United States because it:
options: Resulted in the immediate capture of the South Vietnamese capital of Saigon
Shattered public faith in administration claims that the war was being won, creating a massive 'credibility gap' and intensifying anti-war sentiment
Forced the United States to deploy nuclear weapons in Southeast Asia
Led to the immediate impeachment and removal of General William Westmoreland
questions.explanation: Prior to Tet, the Johnson administration assured the American public that enemy strength was waning and there was 'light at the end of the tunnel'. The simultaneous, coordinated attacks on over 100 South Vietnamese cities and the US Embassy in Saigon broadcast on TV destroyed public confidence and prompted LBJ not to seek re-election.

questions.question: The modern environmental movement gained widespread national momentum in the 1960s primarily sparked by:
options: The immediate economic collapse of the American automotive industry
The passage of the Homestead Act opening Alaskan wilderness to strip mining
The total prohibition of oil extraction on federal lands by executive order
Rachel Carson's publication of Silent Spring (1962), which documented the lethal ecological consequences of synthetic pesticides like DDT

questions.question: President Richard Nixon and National Security Advisor Henry Kissinger pursued the diplomatic strategy of 'détente' primarily to:
options: Ease Cold War tensions through diplomatic negotiations, culminating in historic summits in Beijing and Moscow and the Strategic Arms Limitation Talks (SALT I)
Unilaterally disband the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO)
Form a military alliance with the Soviet Union to invade mainland China
Cut all international trade ties with European and Asian powers
questions.explanation: Détente was a pragmatic realpolitik approach aimed at reducing superpower confrontation. By opening diplomatic relations with communist China in 1972, Nixon exploited the Sino-Soviet split, pressuring Moscow to negotiate arms limitation treaties (SALT I) and trade agreements.

questions.question: The constitutional crisis surrounding the Watergate scandal (1972–1974) and the Supreme Court's ruling in United States v. Nixon affirmed that:
options: The President possesses absolute immunity from congressional subpoena and judicial oversight
The House of Representatives cannot initiate impeachment proceedings against an incumbent president during wartime
Executive privilege is not absolute and cannot be used to withhold evidence relevant to criminal court proceedings, establishing that the President is not above the law
Audio tape recordings made in the Oval Office are the personal private property of the president
questions.explanation: When Nixon cited executive privilege to withhold Oval Office tape recordings from Special Prosecutor Leon Jaworski, the Supreme Court ruled unanimously in U.S. v. Nixon that executive privilege does not shield communications in criminal cases. Facing certain impeachment and conviction, Nixon resigned on August 9, 1974.
